Round 29 options for Bailey

Two proposals from critic round 15 that change screens you see (AGENTS.md rules 9 and 10). Nothing here is built into the game. Frames are the live build with the proposed controls drawn in, in the approved Ink & Gold chrome. Pick, mix, or say none.

A · Accessibility rows in OPTIONS (PR-0032)

Game case: both (shared plumbing: pause screen, SaveData, both presenters). Frames are FFX Chapter I. Today's OPTIONS tab for comparison:

A1 · Reduce motion + Low effects

What it is. Two ON/OFF rows under TEXT SPEED in the pause OPTIONS column, wired to the flags that already exist in SaveData (reduceMotion, lowEffects). Nothing else changes.

What it costs. Smallest: two rows and the presenters read a flag they mostly already read. No new layout work. Does not help low-vision players.

A2 · Those two + Text size (100 / 115 / 130 %)RECOMMENDED

What it is. A1 plus a TEXT SIZE row with three steps, nudged with Left / Right like TEXT SPEED. Grows the battle HUD, dialogue and menus.

What it costs. Medium: real layout work, not one CSS line (the HUD sits on a fixed 640x360 grid; each panel must grow as a unit and the FFX-2 HUD needs its own pass; phone party card caps at 115 %). See docs/concepts/accessibility-2026-09-26 for the 130 % frames.

A3 · Those three + Remap controls

What it is. A2 plus a REMAP CONTROLS row that opens the CONTROLS tab, whose rows become rebindable (Enter on a row, press the new key, swap on conflict, RESET TO DEFAULTS). Hidden on a touch-only phone until a keyboard or pad is used, so the phone frame equals A2.

What it costs. Largest: a rebindable key map in Input and SaveData (migration, conflict swap, reset), a new CONTROLS-tab state, hint strips that read the live map, plus its own test matrix. Pad layout stays fixed.

Recommendation: A2. Text size is the setting that most changes who can read the game (the HUD's smallest type is what the interface checks keep flagging), and A2 adds it for a bounded, already-scoped layout cost. A1 is a fine first step if you want it this week; A3's remapping is the biggest job and helps a smaller group, so it can follow.

B · Paging long command lists on a phone (PR-0218, FFX only)

Game case: FFX only (the FFX command menu and its CTB HUD; FFX-2 has its own battle menu). Today, rows below the sixth are reachable only by an undiscoverable tap-then-Back ladder, and the ▼ mark is inert. Chapter IX Items has 27 rows; Fire Gem is row 19, Poison Fang row 23. Today:

B1 · Real 44 px page buttonsRECOMMENDED

What it is. The inert up/down marks become two 44 px buttons in the ITEMS header with a "1–6 OF 27" counter. Tapping moves the window one page without confirming; a dimmed button means no more that way.

What it costs. Small: the two buttons and a page step in CommandMenu (renderRows / computeMenuWindow), a Playwright tap test. Works for every long list, needs no gesture, and the header has the room (shown between ITEMS and GUIDE).

B2 · Drag-scroll list with a scrollbar thumb

What it is. Drag the grid up or down to scroll it; a slim gold thumb at the right edge shows where you are, with a small "5–10 OF 27 · DRAG LIST" label.

What it costs. Medium: pointer-drag handling that must not steal taps on rows, momentum and snap to rows, a thumb that follows the window, a hint the player may still miss. A 6 px thumb is not a touch target.

Recommendation: B1. It is the fix the critic asked for, it is discoverable at a glance, it gives a real touch target, and it needs no gesture logic that could fight with tapping a row.
